name: TOCH
meaning: torch/fakel: predecessors who did not settle P vs NP but left reusable light

comparison_axes.score_scale: 0 absent, 1 partial/implicit, 2 explicit/central; no total score is treated as truth

canonical_predecessors.source: NSA John Nash Letters; letter received 17 February 1955 and related correspondence
canonical_predecessors.exact_historical_content: Nash models a finite-key binary enciphering process, distinguishes brute-force search over 2^r keys from shortcut attacks, observes that simple ciphers can permit low-degree polynomial shortcuts, and conjectures that sufficiently complex key interactions can make mean key-recovery computation grow exponentially with key length.
canonical_predecessors.what_it_is_not: Not a P vs NP formulation, not an NP-completeness argument, and not a proof of exponential lower bounds.

rigor_signal.formal_object: explicit finite-key process/function and key-length parameter
rigor_signal.falsifiability: a substantially faster general key-recovery method would attack the conjecture
rigor_signal.external_scrutiny: NSA evaluated the proposed cipher and rejected that concrete system for official security requirements

closest_current_nodes: adversarial cost rather than raw state count
interaction structure as possible source of difficulty

surviving_seed.name: INTERACTION_VS_SHORTCUT_COMPLEXITY_SEED
surviving_seed.formalization: For a representation family R_n, distinguish naive state-space cardinality from the minimum exact algorithmic cost after all structure-preserving shortcuts. Measure interaction structure that survives quotienting instead of equating 2^n candidates with 2^n necessary work.

canonical_predecessors.tranception_reverse_pass: Reverse Nash's cryptographic question: rather than asking when interactions force exponential attack cost, ask what exact coordinate change makes those interactions collapse while preserving the decision predicate. This maps naturally to JANUS representation discovery, but carries no theorem by itself.

canonical_predecessors.source: Letter to John von Neumann, 20 March 1956
canonical_predecessors.exact_historical_content: Gödel asks for the optimal worst-case number of steps needed to decide whether a formula has a proof bounded by length n, explicitly wondering whether the growth could be linear or quadratic rather than exhaustive-search-like.
canonical_predecessors.what_it_is_not: The letter predates the formal P/NP vocabulary and does not provide a polynomial algorithm.

rigor_signal.formal_object: Turing machine, formula F, proof-length bound n, worst-case runtime function

surviving_seed.name: CERTIFICATE_DISCOVERY_COST_IS_FIRST_CLASS
surviving_seed.formalization: A short or polynomially verifiable proof object is insufficient; require a uniform polynomial-time constructor/finder under one fixed exponent.

canonical_predecessors.tranception_reverse_pass: Instead of starting with a proof system and asking how fast to search it, JANUS may search for the proof language/representation itself, but the language-selection cost must also be polynomial.

canonical_predecessors.source_kind: historical correspondence summarized in complexity-history literature
canonical_predecessors.exact_historical_content: Raised explicit questions about the complexity of decision procedures, including Tarski-style algebraic decision methods, before complexity theory became a separate field.
canonical_predecessors.what_it_is_not: Not a P vs NP claim.

canonical_predecessors.source: Degree of Difficulty of Computing a Function and a Partial Ordering of Recursive Sets
canonical_predecessors.exact_historical_content: Develops an early formal program for measuring and comparing computational difficulty rather than merely computability.
canonical_predecessors.what_it_is_not: Not P vs NP and not a SAT algorithm.

surviving_seed.name: ORDER_TRANSFORMATIONS_BY_TRUE_RESOURCE_COST
surviving_seed.formalization: Every JANUS representation change must carry a machine-model-independent resource ledger, not only a smaller syntactic state.

canonical_predecessors.source: The Intrinsic Computational Difficulty of Functions
canonical_predecessors.exact_historical_content: Helps establish polynomial time as a robust machine-independent notion of feasible computation.

Gives a polynomial algorithm for maximum matching and explicitly contrasts exponential finite algorithms with algebraic/polynomial growth. Blossom contraction demonstrates that an exponentially large naive search space can collapse through an exact structural transformation.
canonical_predecessors.what_it_is_not: Does not imply all combinatorial search problems have such a contraction.

surviving_seed.name: EXACT_CONTRACTION_BEATS_ENUMERATION
surviving_seed.formalization: Search for polynomially discoverable congruence classes whose contraction preserves the target predicate and supports exact lifted witnesses.

canonical_predecessors.tranception_reverse_pass: Treat every apparent exponential state family as a challenge to discover a blossom-like exact quotient; if no quotient exists, produce the obstruction rather than branching deeper.

canonical_predecessors.exact_historical_content: Establishes SAT as NP-complete, creating the universal reduction boundary for a constructive P=NP route.
Formulates universal search relations with polynomially bounded witnesses and polynomial-time checking, emphasizing search rather than only decision.

surviving_seed.name: SEARCH_RELATION_NOT_JUST_DECISION_BIT
surviving_seed.formalization: Every admitted SAT outcome should preserve a witness relation or independently replayable UNSAT certificate.

canonical_predecessors.exact_historical_content: Builds a network of polynomial reductions among NP-complete problems.
Constructs oracle worlds with opposite P/NP outcomes, proving that relativizing proof techniques alone cannot settle the unrelativized question.
Classifies fixed Boolean constraint languages into tractable and NP-complete cases, showing that the algebra/relations of a problem determine tractability in a precise restricted setting.
canonical_predecessors.what_it_is_not: Does not provide a polynomial decomposition of arbitrary mixed CNFs into tractable languages.

surviving_seed.name: DISCOVER_THE_RIGHT_ALGEBRA_OF_THE_INSTANCE
surviving_seed.formalization: Search for exact preserved operations/relations but charge extensionalization and language-selection cost; mixed-language ambiguity fails closed.

canonical_predecessors.source_kind: claimed P=NP route plus peer-reviewed barrier result
canonical_predecessors.exact_historical_content: Swart pursued polynomial-size LP formulations for Hamiltonian-cycle/TSP-style structure and inferred P=NP. Yannakakis proved exponential lower bounds for symmetric LP formulations of matching and TSP, closing that symmetric formulation route.
canonical_predecessors.what_it_is_not: Yannakakis does not rule out all extended formulations or settle P vs NP.

surviving_seed.name: COMPACT_REPRESENTATION_REQUIRES_EXTENSION_COMPLEXITY_AUDIT
surviving_seed.formalization: Any lifted representation B must prove exact projection/equivalence, polynomial construction, polynomial bit complexity, and polynomial downstream manipulation; symmetry restrictions must be explicit.

canonical_predecessors.tranception_reverse_pass: When a compact representation fails under a symmetry/barrier theorem, search for the precise non-symmetric information that a successful exact representation would need, then charge the cost of discovering that information.

safe_cross_domain_observations: Equilibrium work turns a solution concept into a fixed-point condition; this is a useful adversarial/fixed-point metaphor but not a SAT algorithm.

Embedding work demonstrates exact structure-preserving lifting into a larger representation; this is conceptually close to extension-variable thinking but carries no computational-complexity bound for CNF-SAT.
Cryptography correspondence explicitly treats computational difficulty as the security resource and distinguishes brute force from structural shortcuts.

surviving_seed.name: LIFT_WITH_INVARIANT__THEN_ATTACK_FIXED_POINTS
surviving_seed.formalization: Allow higher-dimensional/lifted representations only when an exact invariant and polynomial construction/manipulation ledger are supplied; treat stable/fixed states as objects for adversarial verification, not as evidence of tractability.

historical_claim_archive.source: Gerhard J. Woeginger P-versus-NP page / maintained mirror
historical_claim_archive.known_scope: 116 listed attempts/milestones through 2016; includes 61 P=NP claims, 49 P!=NP claims, and other outcomes in commonly cited summaries
historical_claim_archive.ingestion_policy: Each claim becomes a claim object plus an algebraic archetype and strongest known attack. No claim is admitted by count, credentials, or rhetoric.
